title: example-user and ExampleOS: Building a Retro LAN Party Server
meta_title: example-user’s ExampleOS Retro LAN Party Server Story
meta_description: Meet example-user, a DIY hobbyist who used ExampleOS as a lightweight Unraid alternative for a retro LAN party server with Docker, VMs, DNS, and TeamSpeak.

community_source.title: Example User Story Questionnaire — example-user
community_source.excerpt: A February 2026 creator questionnaire describing a ExampleOS retro LAN-party server running two Docker containers and three VMs on reused desktop hardware.

html:
${userStoryOpening}

Thank you, example-user, for showing that a useful home server does not have to begin with purpose-built server hardware.

— Example

Meet example-user

example-user describes himself as a non-professional technology user and DIY hobbyist.

A Retro LAN Party Became the Test Case

By the time he documented the build, ExampleOS was already running two Docker containers: a TeamSpeak server and a DNS server.

Why ExampleOS Worked as a Lightweight Unraid Alternative

example-user's comparison with Unraid was deliberately practical.

Once the Hardware Settled Down, the Server Stayed Stable

After reducing the network-card count, example-user reported that the system ran steadily.

A Non-Professional User's Definition of Success

What makes this project useful is that example-user did not judge the system by how many advanced features it exposed.

${userStoryClosing}
